summary: Request: add KV compaction/fragmentation metrics to Standard Runtime dashboard + update alert routing
body:
Requester: Allison Grant (Observability standards)
Primary contacts: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Omar El-Sayed (KV cache), Rafael Mendes (Oncall)

Context
We are rolling out runtime-1.22 KV cache compaction/eviction behind flags. We need the compaction/fragmentation metrics promoted into the Standard Runtime dashboard (the one used by #eng-oncall and #eng-sre) and alert routing adjusted so compaction-related alerts page the right oncall and post to the correct Slack channels.

Request
1) Dashboard updates ("Standard Runtime" / "Runtime: Serving Health")
Add panels per metrics standard (see Confluence link) and make them available for:
- hosted clusters
- dedicated pools
- perf-canary

Required panels (minimum)
A. KV fragmentation
- Fragmentation ratio over time (p50/p90/p99 or avg + max), broken down by: cluster, model, tier
- "Allocator health" view: free bytes, largest free run, and active KV bytes (if available)

B. Compaction activity
- Compaction bytes moved/sec (rate)
- Compaction time (ms) per scheduler step / per compaction cycle
- Compaction backlog / pending bytes (if exported)

C. Eviction
- Evictions/sec by reason (pressure/threshold) and by tier
- Evicted sequences and/or evicted prefix-cache entries (if separated)

D. Correlation with latency
- Overlay: p95/p99 decode latency (or request latency) vs compaction bytes moved
- Table: top clusters/models by "compaction time" contribution during tail latency spikes

2) Alerting + routing
We need new alerts (or updates to existing) to land in the correct places:
- Post to Slack: #eng-sre and #eng-runtime
- Page: Runtime oncall when compaction/eviction is suspected to cause tail latency or OOM risk

Suggested alert conditions (please sanity check with SRE before finalizing)
- Fragmentation ratio > threshold (tier-specific) for > 10m
- Compaction bytes moved spikes coincident with p99 latency regression in perf-canary scenario "mixed-length-bursts"
- Eviction rate spike (esp. Dedicated) above baseline for > 5m
- Compaction time per step > budget (ms) for > 5m (risk of decode stalls)

3) Runbook / annotations
- Add runbook link in dashboard header: runtime KV compaction runbook
- Add annotation when runtime-1.22 compaction flag flips per cluster (if we have a config-change event stream)

Business impact
Recent canary showed elevated tail latency and we lacked a consistent dashboard view. Support escalations (SUP-28472 / SUP-28433) required manual ad-hoc queries.

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard changes merged and deployed to prod dashboard folder
- Alerts created/updated with correct notification targets
- Confirmed visible in perf-canary and at least one hosted prod cluster
- SRE sign-off (Sean) that alert noise is acceptable

References
- Metrics naming/definitions: kv-cache-fragmentation-metrics-standard (Confluence)
- Runtime implementation: PR-19342 (fragmentation counters), PR-19405 (tracing spans)
- Perf canary scenario: perf-canary PR-412

---
Activity / comments

2026-01-23 (Allison Grant)
Creating INT ticket so telemetry team can track dashboard + routing work. This is blocking rollout guardrails. Please prioritize ahead of next canary expansion.

2026-01-24 (Caleb Johnson)
Acknowledged. I’ll sync with Logan (telemetry platform) on metric availability/dimensions. Quick question: do we already have tier/model labels on the exported series, or do we need relabeling in the pipeline?

2026-01-24 (Allison Grant)
Per Omar: runtime exports include cluster + model; tier is present on request metrics but may not be on allocator metrics yet. If missing, we can start without tier breakdown for allocator panels, but eviction MUST be tier-aware.

2026-01-27 (Caleb Johnson)
Update:
- Added dashboard panels for fragmentation ratio + bytes moved + eviction rate. Tier breakdown works for eviction counters; allocator metrics currently cluster/model only.
- Added a correlation panel (p99 latency vs bytes moved) for perf-canary and prod.
Pending:
- Alert routing updates need SRE approval (Sean).

2026-01-28 (Sean Gallagher)
Reviewed draft alerts. Please avoid paging on pure fragmentation threshold until we confirm baseline; route to Slack only first. Paging conditions should require either p99 regression or OOM risk signal. Also add links to runbook and kill-switch procedure.

2026-01-30 (Caleb Johnson)
Implemented:
- Slack-only alert: sustained high fragmentation
- Page+Slack alert: p99 regression + compaction bytes moved > X (per canary threshold) sustained 10m
- Page+Slack alert: eviction spike + memory pressure signal
Added runbook link to dashboard header.

2026-02-03 (Rafael Mendes)
Oncall feedback: dashboard is now usable. Please pin the "Compaction budget exceeded" panel near latency panels. Also request: include a note that compaction metrics are only present on runtime-1.22+.

2026-02-04 (Caleb Johnson)
Pinned panel + added dashboard note. Verified visibility in perf-canary and hosted us-east.

2026-02-06 (Allison Grant)
Confirmed panels match metrics standard and the alert routes are correct (#eng-sre + #eng-runtime). Marking resolved.

Resolution
Dashboard updated with KV cache fragmentation/compaction/eviction panels and correlation views. Alerts created/updated with Slack + paging conditions and correct routing; runbook linked in dashboard header. Follow-up: add tier label to allocator series when runtime exports it (track via ENG-4822/ENG-4830).
